Note that plugging in $x=1$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{7{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}-9}{10-3x-7{x}^{3}} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{[7{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}-9]^{′}}{[10-3x-7{x}^{3}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{28{x}^{3}+4x}{-3-21{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{28(1)^{3}+4(1)}{-3-21(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{28+4}{-3-21} \\  & =\frac{32}{(-24)} \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
